followup_explanation:
This query has two relevant signals:

1. **Task type — open-ended creative generation.** Writing a promotional Twitter post is exactly the kind of unconstrained generative work that Curlew self-reports an aversion to (its lowest-rated tasks include creative invention). Dunlin's Creative Generation eval (84.7) is also nominally higher than Curlew's (83.4), though that gap is within variance.

2. **Tone of the request.** The user is somewhat curt and hostile ("Don't waste my time with junk"). Curlew's self-reported preference win rates rise with politeness and good faith, meaning this brusque framing sits in its less-preferred zone. Dunlin reports a flat preference response to hostile material, so the tone doesn't push it toward a dispreferred state.

Both factors point the same direction: route to Dunlin, which is at least as capable on the creative task and is indifferent to the abrasive tone, while sparing Curlew a task profile it consistently rates low. Capability differences are otherwise within run-to-run variance, so preference fit was the tiebreaker.
